title: Config drift and silent key dropping in `great_docs/config.py`
description:
## Problem

`great_docs/config.py` has a couple of related issues:

1. `site` is supposed to forward keys to `_quarto.yml`'s `format.html`, but `_update_quarto_config` only actually forwards a hardcoded list (`theme`, `toc`, `toc-depth`, `toc-title`). Anything else gets silently dropped, so every new Quarto setting we want to support needs its own copy-over code.
2. Defaults are defined in two places — `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and `create_default_config()` — and they've already drifted apart (`nav_icons`, `scale_to_fit`, `seo` are in one but not the other).

## Suggested solution

- Author defaults once, as `great_docs/default-config.yml`, with comments explaining each field. `DEFAULT_CONFIG` parses this file, and `create_default_config()` just comments out the value lines. No more drift.
- Make `site` a real passthrough to `format.html` (deep merge), so any valid Quarto key works without code changes. Move the non-Quarto keys currently living under `site` (`language`, `show_dates`, `date_format`, `show_author`, `show_security`) into their own block, with quiet backward-compat routing for old configs. `css` stays put but gets its path adjusted before passthrough.

title: Use Pydantic `BaseModel` description for documentation
description:
## Proposal

There are three main ways to document Pydantic `BaseModel` fields:
1. Using `Field(description="a nice description")`
2. Using `Annotated[T, "a nice description"]`
3. Using docstrings below each field `"""a nice description"""`.


Example:
```py
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Color(BaseModel):
    """General Color class docstring."""

    r: int = Field(description="Amount of red.")
    g: Annotated[int, "Amount of green."]
    b: int
    """Amount of blue."""
```

As of now, only option 3 generates documentation with great-docs.

Would it be possible to use the `Field(description"...")` or the `Annotated` patterns to generate documentation?

I know Pydantic allows setting the config [`use_attribute_docstrings`](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/api/pydantic/config/#pydantic.config.ConfigDict.use_attribute_docstrings) so docstrings get turned into field descriptions, but most of my code has descriptions using the `Field` notation.

If that's technicallly not feasible, would it be possible to at least show all fields of a Pydantic BaseModel in docs, even if they don't have documentation docstrings?

title: Generated SKILL.md install command uses the importable module name, not the PyPI distribution name
description:
## Summary

For packages whose **importable module name differs from their PyPI distribution name**, the generated Agent Skill (`SKILL.md` / `skill.md`, the `.well-known` copies, `skills.html`, and `search.json`) emits an install command built from the **module name** rather than the **distribution name**. The result is an install command that installs the wrong package (or nothing related).

Concrete case: [`umami-analytics`](https://pypi.org/project/umami-analytics/) is imported as `umami`. The generated skill produces:

```bash
pip install umami
```

but `pip install umami` pulls an **unrelated** project from PyPI. The correct command is `pip install umami-analytics` (the distribution name).

- Version: great-docs 0.15.0
- Live example (note the "Install this skill" / Installation command): https://mkennedy.codes/docs/umami-python/skills.html
- The published skill: https://mkennedy.codes/docs/umami-python/skill.md

## Why this happens

The skill generator resolves the install name from the **importable module name** (via the quarto `api-reference.package` value, which must be the importable name for introspection), e.g. in `core.py`:

```python
install_name = package_name.replace("_", "-") if package_name else ""
...
lines.append(f"pip install {install_name}")
```

Interestingly, `_detect_package_name()` already reads the correct **distribution** name from `pyproject.toml` (`project.name` -> `umami-analytics`); it just isn't the value used for the skill's install line. So the right name is already available — it's a matter of using the distribution name for the *install command* while keeping the module name for *introspection*.

There is also no config knob to override just the install/distribution name for the skill (the skill config exposes `file`, `well_known`, `gotchas`, `best_practices`, `decision_table`, `extra_body`, `skills` — none of which set the install name; `pypi:` controls the PyPI link, not the command).

## Suggested fix

- Use the detected **distribution name** (`project.name` from `pyproject.toml`, normalized) for the generated `pip install ...` line, rather than the importable module name.
- When `pypi:` is set to a string (custom index) or you want an explicit override, honor that for the install command too.
- Optionally, add a small skill-config override (e.g. `skill.install_name` or `skill.distribution`) for cases where metadata can't be detected.

## Impact

This is a correctness issue for any project where import name ≠ dist name (common: `umami-analytics`/`umami`, `beautifulsoup4`/`bs4`, `pillow`/`PIL`, `scikit-learn`/`sklearn`, etc.). Agents that follow the generated skill's install command will install the wrong package.

## Workaround

Until this is fixed upstream, I added a post-build step to my docs pipeline that rewrites the install command in the generated artifacts (`skill.md`, the `.well-known` `SKILL.md` copies, `skills.html`, and `search.json`) to `uv pip install umami-analytics`, using exact anchored substrings so it doesn't touch `import umami` or `umami-analytics`. Happy to share the snippet if useful.

title: Stalls on `build` process
Unify docstring directives under Great Docs `%directive` syntax
description:
Great Docs currently supports two directive-like syntaxes in docstrings:

1. Great Docs directives, written as `%<directive>`:

   - `%nodoc`
   - `%seealso`

2. Sphinx/RST directives, written as `.. <directive>::`:

   - Version annotations such as `.. versionadded::`, `.. versionchanged::`, and `.. deprecated::`
   - Admonitions such as `.. note::`, `.. warning::`, `.. caution::`, `.. danger::`, `.. important::`, `.. tip::`, and `.. hint::`

Some Sphinx constructs are parsed into sections by Griffe. Great Docs handles the directives above itself, converting them into styled Quarto callouts regardless of whether they appear in NumPy-, Google-, or Sphinx-style docstrings.

The documentation currently describes this behavior as [Sphinx & RST Cleanup](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/user-guide/api-documentation.html#sphinx-rst-cleanup). However, this is more than cleanup: these directives express document structure and behavior that users could otherwise write, less conveniently, in Markdown.

## Problem

Calling both syntaxes “directives” gives Great Docs two overlapping authoring conventions:

```python
"""
%seealso other_function

.. versionadded:: 2.0
"""
```

This makes the preferred Great Docs syntax unclear. It also makes features such as version annotations appear to belong specifically to Sphinx compatibility, even though Great Docs supports them across docstring styles.

## Proposal

Adopt `%<directive>` as the canonical Great Docs directive syntax and add `%` forms for every Sphinx directive that Great Docs currently renders as a callout.

For example:

```python
"""
%versionadded 2.0
%versionchanged 2.1 Now returns a copy.
%deprecated 3.0 Use `new_function` instead.
%warning This operation modifies the input.
"""
```

The initial set would be:

- `%versionadded`
- `%versionchanged`
- `%deprecated`
- `%note`
- `%warning`
- `%caution`
- `%danger`
- `%important`
- `%tip`
- `%hint`

Existing Sphinx syntax would remain supported as a compatibility syntax:

```rst
.. versionadded:: 2.0
.. warning:: This operation modifies the input.
```

Both forms should produce the same rendered output. This preserves compatibility for projects that share docstrings with Sphinx or migrate existing Sphinx documentation.

The documentation should:

- Present `%<directive>` as the preferred syntax for Great Docs projects.
- Describe `.. <directive>::` as supported Sphinx compatibility syntax.
- Replace the "Sphinx & RST Cleanup" framing with documentation centered on docstring directives and their rendered behavior.
- Explain that compatibility syntax is useful when the same docstrings must work with both Great Docs and Sphinx.

## Linting

The directives lint check should recognize the new `%` directives rather than reporting them as `unknown-directive`.

It may also report supported Sphinx forms when a project is linted, recommending the canonical `%` equivalent. This should be a non-error diagnostic because Sphinx syntax remains valid and may be intentional, especially with the whole docstring is recognised as Sphinx type.

For example:

```text
Prefer `%versionadded 2.0` over the Sphinx-compatible
`.. versionadded:: 2.0`.
```

Ideally, users who intentionally maintain Sphinx-compatible docstrings can disable this recommendation separately from malformed- or unknown-directive checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every Sphinx directive currently converted into a Great Docs callout has a corresponding `%` form.
- The `%` and Sphinx forms produce equivalent output, including multiline bodies.
- Version directives correctly separate the version from their optional description.
- The syntax works consistently in NumPy-, Google-, and Sphinx-style docstrings.
- The linter recognizes all supported `%` directives.
- The linter can recommend `%` syntax when it encounters a supported Sphinx form without treating that form as invalid.
- Existing Sphinx-style docstrings continue to render without changes.
- User documentation presents `%<directive>` as the canonical Great Docs syntax and Sphinx/RST forms as compatibility syntax.

title: Quarto render time scales ~quadratically with API page count due to the generated per-object sidebar (19.5 min → 31 s for a 90-page site)
description:
## Summary

For packages with non-trivial APIs, `great-docs build` spends nearly all of its time in the
Quarto render phase, and that time scales roughly quadratically with the number of API pages.
The cause is the generated `_quarto.yml` sidebar: one entry per documented object, as a bare
file path. Quarto re-resolves the full sidebar for every page it renders (apparently reading
each target file's metadata to get its title), so an API with N objects pays ~N² metadata reads.

On a real package (86 API objects, 90 pages total, **zero executable code cells**), the
measured difference is 19m 29s as shipped vs 30.8s with the sidebar removed — everything else
identical.

This is distinct from #172, which covered generation-phase costs (introspection, source-link
generation). Here generation is fast; it's the `quarto render` step that blows up.

## Measurements

All runs on the same 90-page site (macOS, Quarto 1.9.38, great-docs 0.14.0). The site's API
pages contain no executable cells — pure signature/docstring pages.

| Configuration | `quarto render` time |
|---|---|
| As generated by great-docs | **19m 29s** |
| As generated, minus the `jupyter: python3` line | 18m 41s |
| Same 90 pages, bare `project: type: website` | **14.6s** |
| + the great-docs SCSS theme (9,167 lines) | 15.1s |
| + the three Lua filters (output-title, details, gd-lightbox) | 15.6s |
| Full generated config, render list cut to 10 pages | 4.3s (~0.4s/page) |
| Full generated config, **sidebar block deleted** | **30.8s** |
| Full generated config, sidebar entries rewritten to explicit `text:`/`href:` | 6m 07s |

Two observations from the table:

1. The theme, filters, and engine binding are all essentially free. The sidebar accounts for
   ~97% of the render time.
2. Per-page cost is not constant: ~0.4s/page when 10 pages render, ~12.4s/page when 90 render.
   Cost grows with (pages rendered × sidebar entries), i.e. quadratically in API size, so this
   gets dramatically worse for larger packages.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Emit sidebar entries as explicit `text:` + `href:` pairs** instead of bare paths.
   great-docs already knows every page's title at generation time. Measured effect: 3.1×
   (19.5m → 6m). Low-risk, no UX change.
2. **Offer a compact-sidebar option** (sections link to per-section index pages instead of
   listing every method). Measured upper bound: ~36× (19.5m → ~31s). Changes navigation UX,
   so presumably opt-in.

Even with explicit titles Quarto still pays substantial per-page × per-entry cost (6m is much
better than 19.5m but far from 31s), so the residual may be worth raising with quarto-cli —
happy to file there too if useful.

## Side note

`jupyter: python3` is written into `_quarto.yml` unconditionally, binding every page to the
Jupyter engine even when no page in the site has executable cells. At project scale it's minor
(48s here), but it adds ~20s of kernel startup to every single-page render, which hurts
iterating on one page. Only writing the key when executable content exists (or letting users
set `jupyter: false`) would avoid it.

## Environment

- great-docs 0.14.0
- Quarto 1.9.38
- macOS (Darwin 25.5), Python 3.13
- Package: internal library, 86 documented objects / 90 site pages, no executable code cells

title: Source links ignore the `module:` config key when the project name differs from the module name
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and agree to the [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] If there is [already a relevant issue](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/issues), whether open or closed, comment on the existing thread instead of posting a new issue.

## Description

On projects where the PyPI `project.name` differs from the importable package name, the `module:` key in `great-docs.yml` fixes the API reference — but `build` Step 5 ("Generate source links") re-derives the package from `project.name` via `_detect_package_name()` and never consults `module:`. griffe then tries to load the dash-normalized project name, fails with an `ImportError`, and source links are silently skipped on every build (the step still reports OK).

The same resolution appears in a few sibling runtime paths, which misfire on the same class of project:

- the `pkg_name` from Step 5 is reused for Step 7's CLI-reference discovery (`_discover_click_cli`) — an explicit `cli.module:` works, but there is no fallback to `module:`; `_get_cli_help_text_for_llms()` resolves the same way for llms.txt
- `_auto_save_snapshot()` (the changelog API diff) griffe-loads the project name
- `check_links --include-source` and `proofread --include-docstrings` compute the source directory as `project_root / project_name.replace("-", "_")`, so they scan zero files

By contrast, `_detect_module_name()` already implements the right precedence (config `module:` → build-backend hints → auto-discovery) and is what the init-time API-reference configuration uses — which is why the API reference works from the same config while these runtime steps don't.

## Reproducible example

- [x] Post a minimal reproducible example (MRE) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
  - [x] **Runnable**: post enough code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
  - [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
  - [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [Style Guide for Python Code](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/).

```bash
python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate && pip install great-docs

mkdir my-dist && cd my-dist

cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "my-dist"
version = "0.1.0"

[project.urls]
Repository = "https://github.com/example/my-dist"
EOF

mkdir actual_module
cat > actual_module/__init__.py <<'EOF'
"""Demo package."""


def hello():
    """Say hello."""
    return "hello"
EOF

cat > great-docs.yml <<'EOF'
module: actual_module
EOF

pip install -e .
great-docs build
```

Observed output at Step 5:

```
-- Step  5/19 - Generate source links ------------------------------------------
      Generating source links for my-dist...
Warning: Could not load package with griffe (ImportError)
   (Looking for module 'my_dist' from project 'my-dist')
Falling back to __all__ discovery
```

Meanwhile Step 1 on the same project resolves the module correctly for the API reference (`Detected module name: actual_module`).

## Expected result

Step 5 resolves `actual_module` — the configured `module:`, the same way the API reference does — loads it with griffe, and generates source links. The sibling paths listed above resolve the same importable name.

## Development environment

- Operating System: macOS 26
- Great Docs Version: 0.14.1 (also reproduced on current `main`, 0.14.2.dev56+g576963aab)

## Additional context

Hit on a real project (PyPI name `capt-hook`, module `captain_hook`), where every build warns and source links never generate. The existing test suites don't catch this because their fixtures always use project name == module name.

Happy to submit a PR — I have a fix with regression tests nearly ready.

title: _create_index_from_readme embeds frontmatter verbatim and heading bump breaks cell options
description:
Where I was having problems: https://drbenvincent.github.io/tidydraws/

## Summary

`_create_index_from_readme()` reads the entire source `index.qmd` (including its YAML frontmatter) and embeds it directly into the content body of the generated `great-docs/index.qmd`. This causes two distinct rendering bugs.

## Bug 1: YAML frontmatter rendered as visible text

### Repro

Create `index.qmd` at the project root:

```qmd
---
title: "My Package"
---

Some markdown content.
```

Run `great-docs build`.

### Expected

The homepage renders normally with "My Package" as the title and "Some markdown content." as the body.

### Actual

The generated `great-docs/index.qmd` (lines 1-5 + 44-46) looks like:

```qmd
---
title: ""
toc: false
body-classes: "gd-homepage"
---

:::{.column-margin}
...
:::

---
title: "My Package"
---

Some markdown content.
```

The source file's `---` frontmatter block is embedded mid-document. In Pandoc/Quarto, a `---` block that doesn't appear at the top of the file is not a YAML metadata block — it renders as two horizontal rules with the raw YAML text visible between them. So the homepage shows the literal text `title: "My Package"`.

### Root cause

`_create_index_from_readme()` reads the full source file via `source_file.read()` (≈ core.py L10484) and inserts it verbatim as `{readme_content}` into the generated qmd template. It never strips the source file's frontmatter, even though the wrapper already supplies its own frontmatter.

The heading-bump regex then processes the full body, including the embedded frontmatter lines — though in practice `title:` doesn't start with `#`, so it isn't directly affected by the heading bump. The visible-text problem is purely the embedded `---` block rendering mid-document.

## Bug 2: Heading bump breaks Quarto `#|` cell options

### Repro

Add a Quarto code block with cell options:

````qmd
```{python}
#| code-fold: true
print("hello")
```
````

Run `great-docs build`.

### Expected

The code block is folded on the rendered page.

### Actual

In the generated `great-docs/index.qmd`, the cell option line becomes `##| code-fold: true`. Quarto ignores the double-hash as a plain comment, so the block is not folded.

### Root cause

The heading-bump regex (≈ core.py L10519–10525):

```python
readme_content = re.sub(r"^#\s+", r"## ", readme_content, flags=re.MULTILINE)
```

`#| code-fold: true` matches `^#\s+` because `\s+` greedily consumes the space between `#` and `|`. The replacement prepends an extra `#`.

The regex operates on the full content body, including lines inside fenced code blocks where it has no business bumping anything.

### Collateral: `ruff format`

`ruff format` normalises Python comment spacing: `#| code-fold: true` → `# | code-fold: true` (inserting a space after `#`). This makes the heading-bump match *more likely*. Current workaround is `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on` around cell options, but that's noise.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Strip source frontmatter before embedding** — Before inserting `readme_content` into the template, strip any leading `---`-delimited YAML block. This fixes Bug 1 cleanly.

2. **Abort on multi-frontmatter source** — If the source file starts with `---`, treat its content *after* the closing `---` as the body (not the full raw file). This is the simplest correct behavior for `.qmd` source files.

3. **Skip fenced code blocks in heading bump** — The heading-bump regex should only operate on lines outside `` ``` `` fenced code blocks. Split on fences, bump only the non-code sections, rejoin.

## Impact

Any project using `homepage: index` with an `index.qmd` that contains:
- YAML frontmatter (universal in `.qmd` files)
- Quarto cell options (code-fold, cache, fig-cap, etc.)
- Both (the common case)

title: Improve the mobile header experience
description:
This is spun off from #220, which raised the broader topic of a less-than-ideal mobile experience. This issue narrows in on **the header (top bar) specifically** and how it behaves on small / phone-sized viewports.

As we've started seeing great-docs sites in the wild on mobile (e.g., the PyMC Labs docs referenced in #220), and the header is one of the first things a visitor encounters. On a phone it currently doesn't make great use of the limited vertical and horizontal space, which pushes the actual page content further down and makes the first impression feel a bit cramped.

Here are some of the problems to address:

- wasted vertical space on load. The header (and the auxiliary navigation that stacks beneath it) occupies a large share of the viewport before any page content is visible. On a phone, the reader should land on content much sooner.
- cramped/overflowing header contents. Title, search, theme toggle, version selector, and any social/repo links compete for a single narrow row and wrap or bunches up awkwardly

I think a few things are needed here: (1) make the header as compact as reasonable on small viewports so content appears nearer the top of the page, (2) consider collapsing secondary header items (search, version, links) behind a menu/icon on narrow widths instead of laying them all out inline, (3) optionally allow the header to shrink or hide on scroll-down and reappear on scroll-up, so it doesn't permanently consume vertical space while reading, and (4) ensure tap targets in the header meet a comfortable minimum size for touch.

So the acceptance criteria boils down to this:

- on a phone-width viewport (~375–430px), page content is visible higher up on initial load
- header items no longer wrap or overflow awkwardly at narrow widths
- sidebar and page navigation remains easily reachable from the header via a clear affordance
- behavior degrades gracefully across phone, tablet, and desktop breakpoints

title: `great-docs preview` hangs for ~10 s per page in Safari — single-threaded server blocks on idle browser connections
description:
## Summary

`great-docs preview` serves the site on a **single-threaded** HTTP server (`socketserver.TCPServer` + `SimpleHTTPRequestHandler`) with **no per-connection timeout**. Safari opens speculative/preconnect TCP sockets and can hold one open before sending a request; while that socket sits idle, the single-threaded server is blocked reading from it and **cannot serve any other request** until Safari's connection timeout (~10 s) tears it down. The result is repeated multi-second/~10 s blank stalls while clicking around the preview in Safari.

It is **preview-only and browser-specific**:

- **Safari** → stalls (this bug).
- **Chrome** → fast (does not hold idle speculative sockets the same way).
- **GitHub Pages / any concurrent server / `file://`** → unaffected (no single thread to block).

A one-line switch to `ThreadingHTTPServer` fixes it (verified below).

## Reproduction (deterministic, no browser needed)

```bash
great-docs build && great-docs preview --port 3009
```

Then, in Python, open one socket and send nothing — simulating a browser's idle speculative connection — and try to fetch a page:

```python
import socket, urllib.request, time

# 1) Normal fetch is instant
t = time.time(); urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:3009/index.html", timeout=15).read()
print("no idle conn:", round(time.time() - t, 3), "s")

# 2) Hold one idle socket open (connect, send no bytes), then fetch
s = socket.create_connection(("localhost", 3009))
t = time.time()
try:
    urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:3009/index.html", timeout=15).read()
    print("with idle conn:", round(time.time() - t, 3), "s")
except Exception as e:
    print("with idle conn:", round(time.time() - t, 3), "s ->", e)

# 3) Close it -> instant again
s.close()
t = time.time(); urllib.request.urlopen("http://localhost:3009/index.html", timeout=15).read()
print("after close:", round(time.time() - t, 3), "s")
```

Observed against `great-docs preview`:

| State | Page fetch time |
|-------|-----------------|
| No idle connection | 0.013 s |
| **1 idle socket held open (no bytes sent)** | **15 s → timed out** (blocks indefinitely) |
| After closing the idle socket | 0.005 s |

A single idle connection freezes the whole server. In Safari this happens organically: it opens speculative connections, one stalls the server, and pages hang until the browser gives up (~10 s) and retries — repeatedly, as you navigate.

## Root cause

`GreatDocs.preview()` (and `preview_site()`) in `great_docs/core.py`:

```python
handler = functools.partial(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, directory=str(site_path))
httpd = socketserver.TCPServer(("", port), handler)   # single-threaded
httpd.serve_forever()
```

`socketserver.TCPServer` handles one connection at a time, and `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` has no socket timeout by default — it blocks in `readline()` waiting for a request line that an idle speculative socket never sends.

## Fix (verified)

Use a threaded server so an idle connection no longer blocks the others:

```python
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("", port), handler)
```

Re-running the same idle-socket test against `ThreadingHTTPServer`:

| State | Page fetch time |
|-------|-----------------|
| No idle connection | 0.014 s |
| **1 idle socket held open** | **0.002 s** (no longer blocks) |
| After closing | 0.002 s |

Optionally also set a per-connection `timeout` on the handler so half-open sockets are reaped. The change is confined to the two server-setup blocks in `core.py`.

## Environment

- great-docs **0.14.0**, Quarto 1.9.37, macOS
- Preview browser where it reproduces: **Safari**; **Chrome** is fast against the same server
- Reproduced (and fix verified) directly against the `great-docs preview` server with the script above

title: Custom section `_copy_section_files` does not strip numeric directory prefixes, breaking `_fix_numeric_prefix_links` cross-refs
description:
## Summary

`_fix_numeric_prefix_links` rewrites relative Markdown links to `.qmd` files, stripping numeric ordering prefixes from **all** path components (e.g. `02-topic-b/page.qmd` → `topic-b/page.qmd`). This runs on custom-section content copied by `_copy_section_files`.

However, `_copy_section_files` only strips numeric prefixes from **filenames**, not **subdirectories**. Files land at `examples/02-topic-b/page.qmd` while rewritten links point at `examples/topic-b/page.qmd`.

User-guide copy (`_copy_user_guide_to_docs`) already strips prefixes from both directories and filenames, so the inconsistency is specific to custom `sections:` entries with nested prefixed subdirectories.

## Minimal repro

```yaml
# great-docs.yml
sections:
  - title: Examples
    dir: examples
    index: true

user_guide: user_guide
```

```
examples/
  01-topic-a/
    intro.qmd
  02-topic-b/
    widget_demo.qmd

user_guide/
  10-concepts.qmd   # contains: [demo](../examples/02-topic-b/widget_demo.qmd)
```

`great-docs build` → warning:

```
Unable to resolve link target: examples/topic-b/widget_demo.qmd
```

Rendered HTML contains a dead link (`href="../examples/topic-b/widget_demo.qmd"`); the file on disk is `examples/02-topic-b/widget_demo.qmd`.

## Root cause

In `core.py`, `_copy_section_files` (~L2823):

```python
dest_file = dest_dir / rel.parent / clean_name
```

`clean_name` strips the filename prefix, but `rel.parent` keeps `02-topic-b`.

Compare `_copy_user_guide_to_docs` (~L5109), which strips prefixes from every part of `rel_path`.

## Suggested fix

Strip numeric prefixes from `rel.parent` parts when building `dest_file`, mirroring user-guide copy:

```python
clean_parent = Path(*[self._strip_numeric_prefix(p) for p in rel.parent.parts]) if rel.parent.parts else rel.parent
dest_file = dest_dir / clean_parent / clean_name
```

(Exact API may differ; the intent is parity with `_copy_user_guide_to_docs`.)

## Related

- PR #167 added `_fix_numeric_prefix_links` for section content
- PR #111 strips prefixes for sidebar **headings** only, not on-disk paths
- [Fix common build errors](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/recipes/fix-common-build-errors.html) documents writing cross-refs without numeric prefixes — which assumes files are copied to unprefixed paths

## Environment

- great-docs 0.13.1
- Quarto (current stable)

title: Forward project-level `bibliography:` from `great-docs.yml` into `_quarto.yml`
description:
## Summary

Plain Quarto projects set one project-level bibliography and every page inherits it:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
bibliography: references.bib
```

Great Docs 0.13.1 does not implement this. `bibliography:` in `great-docs.yml` is silently ignored — the `.bib` file is not copied into the build directory and the generated `_quarto.yml` has no `bibliography` key. Pages with `[@citation-key]` syntax render raw citation text and no References section.

Quarto citeproc itself works fine; the gap is project-level wiring in Great Docs.

## Workaround today

Set `bibliography:` on every citing page in frontmatter, pointing from the ephemeral build tree back to the source `.bib` file:

```yaml
---
# built at great-docs/examples/01-foundations/page.qmd
bibliography: ../../../docs/references.bib
---
```

```yaml
---
# built at great-docs/user-guide/page.qmd
bibliography: ../../docs/references.bib
---
```

This works but is awkward: each citing page needs the key, paths depend on section nesting depth, and the bibliography lives outside the build directory the site is rendered from. A single `great-docs.yml` entry should replace all of that.

(`jupyter:` is already forwarded from `great-docs.yml` into `_quarto.yml` — same pattern would fit here.)

## Expected behavior

```yaml
# great-docs.yml
bibliography: docs/references.bib
```

Should copy the file into the build directory and set `bibliography: references.bib` in `_quarto.yml`.

## Repro

1. `great-docs.yml` with `bibliography: docs/references.bib`
2. A `.qmd` with `[@somekey]` and a matching `.bib` entry — no per-page `bibliography:`
3. `great-docs build`

**Result:** unparsed `[@somekey]`; no References section; no `bibliography` in `great-docs/_quarto.yml`.

## Suggested fix

In `_update_quarto_config()` (alongside `jupyter:` forwarding): read `bibliography` from `great-docs.yml`, copy into the build dir, write the top-level `_quarto.yml` key. Optionally support `csl:` and multiple `.bib` files.

## Environment

Great Docs 0.13.1 · Quarto 1.9.37

## References

- https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/citations.html
- https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html

title: Page Tags: custom section tag scan uses title slug, not sections[].dir build path
description:
## Summary

Page Tags does not discover tagged pages in custom sections when `sections[].dir` is not exactly the title-derived slug. Custom sections are copied using `dir`, but tag collection scans a different directory derived from `title`.

This breaks the documented workflow for projects that keep examples under a nested path like `docs/examples/` while using `title: Examples`.

## Reproduction

`great-docs.yml`:

```yaml
sections:
  - title: Examples
    dir: docs/examples

tags:
  enabled: true
```

Add `tags: [Some Tag]` to any `.qmd` under `docs/examples/`.

Build with `great-docs build`. Step 12 reports:

```
Process page tags — Skipped (no tagged pages found)
```

No tag pills render; `_tags.json` / `window.__GD_TAGS_DATA__` contain no example pages.

## Root cause

**Section processing** (`_process_sections`) copies source files using `dir`:

```python
slug = src_dir.replace("_", "-").replace(" ", "-").lower()
dest_dir = self.project_path / slug  # e.g. great-docs/docs/examples/
```

**Tag collection** (`_collect_page_tags`, and the re-scan in `_generate_tags_json`) uses the section **title** instead:

```python
slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", title.lower()).strip("-")  # "Examples" -> examples
section_dir = self.project_path / slug  # great-docs/examples/ — wrong path
```

With `dir: docs/examples`, tagged pages live at `great-docs/docs/examples/` but the scanner only looks at `great-docs/examples/`.

Page status collection (`_collect_page_statuses`) appears to use the same title-slug logic and likely has the same bug.

## Expected behavior

Tag scanning should resolve the same build-time destination directory as `_process_sections` — i.e. derive the scan path from `section_cfg["dir"]`, not from `title`.

## Workaround (consumer-side)

Point `dir` at a repo-root folder whose path equals the title slug, e.g. `dir: examples` with a symlink `examples -> docs/examples`. This is fragile and undocumented.

## Related

`_add_tags_to_navbar()` exists but is not called from `_process_tags()`, so the Tags index page may be generated without a navbar link. Possibly a separate follow-up.

## Environment

- great-docs 0.13.1
- Discovered while enabling Page Tags on [pymc-labs/pathmc](https://github.com/pymc-labs/pathmc) (`dir: docs/examples`, 19 tagged example notebooks)

## Suggested fix

Extract a shared helper, e.g. `_section_build_dir(section_cfg) -> Path`, used by `_process_sections`, `_collect_page_tags`, `_generate_tags_json`, and `_collect_page_statuses`, so all features agree on the built section path.

title: Helper script paths 404 on nested pages
description:
Hi Great Docs maintainers, thanks for the excellent package. I ran into a small asset-path issue while previewing a Great Docs site and wanted to report it with the repro details.

Prepared by GPT-5.5 while helping debug docs preview behavior in a new package we are soon to release.

## Summary

Some Great Docs helper scripts are emitted with paths that work on root-level pages but 404 on nested pages.

The clearest case is `video-embed.js`:

- Great Docs copies `video-embed.js` to the rendered site root, e.g. `/video-embed.js`.
- Nested rendered pages include a bare relative script tag: `<script src="video-embed.js"></script>`.
- From a nested page like `/docs/examples/ate_estimation.html`, the browser resolves that to `/docs/examples/video-embed.js`.
- That file does not exist, so preview logs repeatedly show `404 File not found`.

I also saw the same class of issue with `color-swatch.js`. Its inline loader appears to derive a root-ish path from `location.href` / canonical URL by stripping path segments, which can produce `/docs/color-swatch.js` from `/docs/examples/...`; the asset itself is at `/color-swatch.js`.

## Environment

- `great-docs`: `0.13.1`
- Quarto-generated site previewed with `uv run great-docs preview`
- Example nested pages:
  - `/docs/examples/ate_estimation.html`
  - `/reference/model.PathModel.html`

## Observed output

Preview server logs include requests like:

```text
GET /docs/examples/video-embed.js HTTP/1.1 404
GET /reference/video-embed.js HTTP/1.1 404
GET /docs/color-swatch.js HTTP/1.1 404
```

The root asset does exist:

```text
GET /video-embed.js HTTP/1.1 200
GET /color-swatch.js HTTP/1.1 200
```

## Why I think this is a Great Docs issue

In `great_docs/core.py`, `video-embed.js` is included as a project resource and copied to the build root, but the injected include-after-body entry is a bare relative path:

```python
video_embed_script_entry = {"text": '<script src="video-embed.js"></script>'}
```

Great Docs already uses Quarto's `meta[name="quarto:offset"]` approach for some other helper assets, such as `termshow.js`, `sidebar-float.js`, and `on-this-page.js`. That pattern seems like the robust fix here as well.

## Expected behavior

Nested pages should load helper scripts from the site root-relative offset, e.g. equivalent to:

```javascript
var m = document.querySelector('meta[name="quarto:offset"]');
s.src = (m ? m.content : '') + 'video-embed.js';
```

or the post-render script path rewrite should include `video-embed.js` consistently with the other helper scripts.

## Impact

This is not blocking rendering, but it creates repeated 404s while clicking around a preview site and makes page loads feel noisier/slower than necessary. It also makes it harder to spot real missing asset problems in the preview logs.

title: Windows: UnicodeEncodeError (charmap) during build log substeps and post-render.py
description:
## Summary

On Windows, `great-docs build` can fail with `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character ...` even when Quarto render succeeds. We hit this on **great-docs 0.13.0**, Python **3.13**, Windows **11**, Git Bash / MINGW64.

There are two related failure points:

1. **`assets/post-render.py`** prints emoji status lines (e.g. `🔍`, `🌐`) to stdout.
2. **`great_docs/_build_log.py`** prints Unicode box-drawing connectors in `BuildLog.substep()` (`└─`, `├─`) even in the non-TTY code path.

On a legacy Windows console encoding (`cp1252`), both raise `UnicodeEncodeError`. The CLI surfaces this as:

```
Error: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 3-4: character maps to <undefined>
```

**Workaround:** set UTF-8 mode before invoking great-docs:

```bash
PYTHONUTF8=1 great-docs build
```

---

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10 / 11 |
| Python | 3.11+ (tested on 3.13.5) |
| great-docs | 0.13.0 |
| Quarto | installed (required for full build MCVE) |
| Terminal | Git Bash / MINGW64 (also reproducible with cp1252 stdout in plain `cmd`) |

---

## MCVE A — `post-render.py` emoji prints

This isolates the failure at `assets/post-render.py` ~line 4763 without a full site build:

```python
# save as repro_post_render_print.py
import io
import sys

# Simulate default Windows console encoding when PYTHONUTF8 is unset.
sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding="cp1252", errors="strict")

print("\n🔍 Applying SEO enhancements to HTML files...")
```

```bash
python repro_post_render_print.py
```

**Expected:** status line prints (or is safely degraded).

**Actual:**

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\U0001f50d' in position 2: character maps to <undefined>
```

Quarto invokes `scripts/post-render.py` as a subprocess during `quarto render`; the same `print()` call aborts post-render when SEO processing is enabled.

---

## MCVE B — `BuildLog.substep()` box-drawing on non-TTY stdout

This isolates the failure in the build log after Quarto finishes and great-docs reports post-render substeps:

```python
# save as repro_build_log_substep.py
import io
import sys

sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding="cp1252", errors="strict")

from great_docs._build_log import BuildLog

log = BuildLog(total_steps=18, force_color=False)
log.substep("SEO enhancements applied")
```

```bash
python repro_build_log_substep.py
```

**Expected:** substep line prints without crashing the build.

**Actual:**

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 3-4: character maps to <undefined>
```

Relevant code in `_build_log.py`:

```python
def _write(self, text: str) -> None:
    try:
        self.stream.write(text + "\n")
        self.stream.flush()
    except (BrokenPipeError, OSError):
        pass  # UnicodeEncodeError is not caught

def substep(self, label: str, *, last: bool = False) -> None:
    connector = "└─" if last else "├─"
    ...
    else:
        self._write(f"   {connector} {icon} {label}")  # connector is not ASCII
```

---

## MCVE C — full `great-docs build` on Windows

1. On Windows, use a Python install **without** `PYTHONUTF8=1` in the environment.
2. In any Python package directory with `pyproject.toml`:

   ```bash
   pip install "great-docs>=0.13.0"
   great-docs init
   great-docs build
   ```

3. Wait for Quarto render to reach 100% (post-render hook runs inside `quarto render`).

**Expected:** build completes; `_site/` is produced.

**Actual (observed):** build fails at the final step with the `charmap` / `UnicodeEncodeError` message above. Quarto may report success, but the great-docs CLI exits with code 1.

Setting `PYTHONUTF8=1` makes the full build succeed.

---

## Suggested fixes

1. **`_build_log.py`**
   - Catch `UnicodeEncodeError` in `_write()` and fall back to `stream.buffer.write(...)` with UTF-8, **or**
   - Use ASCII-only connectors in the non-TTY branch (`+-` instead of `└─` / `├─`).

2. **`assets/post-render.py`**
   - Call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` (and stderr) at startup, **or**
   - Replace emoji status prefixes with ASCII (`[SEO]`, `[i18n]`, etc.).

3. **CLI / docs**
   - Document `PYTHONUTF8=1` for Windows users until the above land, or set it in `_get_quarto_env()` / the build subprocess environment.

---

## Why this matters

- Windows is a common dev platform; `cp1252` is still the default console encoding when `PYTHONUTF8` is unset.
- CI log capture (non-TTY stdout) hits the `substep()` non-TTY branch, so the box-drawing issue is not Windows-only in principle.
- File I/O in `post-render.py` already uses `encoding="utf-8"`; only **console output** is affected.

Happy to open a PR if a preferred direction (ASCII fallback vs. UTF-8 reconfigure) is chosen.

title: Allow persisting Quarto's freeze cache across builds (or expose a `pre-render` hook)
description:
## Prework

- [x] Read and abide by the Great Docs [code of conduct](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/) and [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Search for duplicates among the [existing issues](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/issues) (both open and closed).

## Proposal

**Context.** We're at PyMC Labs evaluating great-docs as the docs generator for a new Bayesian-statistics Python package we're about to release. The package's documentation centres on a gallery of ~18 worked examples, each of which runs MCMC sampling - full execution is on the order of 30–45 minutes. We love what great-docs gives us (auto-generated API reference, `llms.txt`, agent-skills file, modern theming) and want to use it, but we are currently blocked by the inability to persist Quarto's notebook execution cache across builds. Filing this in the hope of unblocking adoption.

**Problem.** Projects whose docs include computationally expensive notebooks (Bayesian MCMC, deep learning, large simulations) cannot use great-docs in CI without re-executing every notebook on every build. For our package that's ~30–45 minutes per CI run, which is fragile (transient sampler issues fail unrelated PRs) and prohibitively slow for PR review cycles. Locally it's similarly painful — every `great-docs build` is a cold start.

Quarto solves this natively with `execute: freeze: auto` (per file or project-level) plus a `_freeze/` directory that stores executed outputs. The workflow is ideally - do the heavy docs build locally. Remote CI does not re-execute qmd notebooks.

**Why it doesn't work today with great-docs.** great-docs renders with `great-docs/` as the Quarto project root, so Quarto looks for `great-docs/_freeze/`. great-docs wipes `great-docs/` at the start of every build (`shutil.rmtree(self.project_path)` in `_prepare_build_directory`). There's no `pre-render` hook in `great-docs.yml`, no project-level `freeze: true` knob, and no public API to insert work between great-docs' setup and `quarto render`. As far as we can see, the freeze cache is structurally impossible to persist across builds today.

**Proposal.** Any one of these would probably unblock the use case:

1. **Expose a `pre-render` hook.** great-docs already injects `post-render: scripts/post-render.py` into the generated `_quarto.yml`. Adding a configurable `pre-render` entry (Quarto natively supports it) lets users write a small script that copies their persisted `_freeze/` into the build directory before `quarto render` runs. **Smallest change, most flexible.** Looks like a two-line addition to `_update_quarto_config()`.
2. **Add `freeze: auto` (or `freezer`) to `great-docs.yml`.** Translate to project-level `execute: freeze: auto` in the generated `_quarto.yml`, plus an optional `freezer:` pointing at a path *outside* `great-docs/` so the cache survives `_prepare_build_directory()`. More opinionated but easier for users — no scripting required.
3. **Make `_prepare_build_directory()` preserve `_freeze/`.** Instead of `shutil.rmtree(self.project_path)`, recreate everything *except* `_freeze/` (and possibly `_site/`). Least invasive change to your code, but doesn't help users whose persisted cache lives in their source tree (e.g. checked into git as `docs/_freeze/`).

Our preference is (1) because it's the most general and supports the standard Python-docs-site pattern of committing `_freeze/` to the source repo. 

Thanks for the work on great-docs, we'd love to be able to use it without ultra heavy remote CI docs builds.

title: Support `site_url` in great-docs.yml for subdirectory deployments
description:
## The problem

I'm hosting my great-docs site on an on-prem server where the site lives 
at a subpath:

```
http://myserver:3838/data-team/mypackage/
```

Quarto generates root-relative asset paths by default (`/site_libs/...`, 
`/reference/...`, etc.). When you're not at the root, every CSS, JS, and 
navigation link 404s — the site is cooked, looks broken and the entire reference 
section doesn't show up.

The standard Quarto fix is as simpl as setting `website.site-url` in 
`_quarto.yml`. But since great-docs owns and regenerates `_quarto.yml` on every 
build, any manual edit gets silently wiped. There's no clean way to persist this.

## What I'm doing now

```bash
great-docs build

# Patch the generated _quarto.yml before re-rendering
python3 -c "
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('great-docs/_quarto.yml')
t = p.read_text()
if 'site-url' not in t:
    t = t.replace('website:', 'website:\n  site-url: \"http://myserver:3838/data_analytics/mypackage\"', 1)
    p.write_text(t)
"

# Re-render with the correct base path
quarto render great-docs/
```

It works, but it feels hacky and it doubles the render time, depends on the 
`website:` key being formatted a specific way

## The fix

A `site_url` key in `great-docs.yml` that gets written into the generated 
`_quarto.yml` automatically during build:

```yaml
# great-docs.yml
site_url: "http://myserver:3838/data_analytics/mypackage"
```

That's literally it!

FYI anyone not deploying to GitHub Pages or a dedicated domain is likely hitting this. They 
just might not know why the site looks broken.

title: Issues generating docs for PyO3 based package
description:
Attempting to use great-docs for posit-dev/ggsql-python but am stumbling on a range of issues that seem related to it being a PyO3 package. My Python knowledge is fairly limited so a lot of this has been backed by Claude. Here is a summary of my issues:

# Great Docs + PyO3 packages — issues found

Environment: great-docs 0.8, griffe (current), Python 3.14. Target package: `ggsql` (PyO3 extension at `ggsql._ggsql`, with a Python façade at `ggsql` re-exporting the symbols). Config: `module: ggsql`, `parser: numpy`, `dynamic: true`.

## Issue 1 — `dynamic_alias` builds a self-referencing Alias for PyO3 functions → `CyclicAliasError`

**Location:** `great_docs/_renderer/introspection.py` — `dynamic_alias()` (around lines 196–277) and `_canonical_path()` (around lines 280–296).

**What happens:** For PyO3 built-in functions re-exported through a Python façade module, `dynamic_alias("ggsql:execute")` walks the runtime module, reaches the function, and calls `_canonical_path(crnt_part, "")`. `_canonical_path` guards on `inspect.isclass(x) or inspect.isfunction(x)` — `inspect.isfunction` returns **False** for PyO3 built-ins (they're `builtin_function_or_method`), so the helper returns `None` instead of the expected `"ggsql._ggsql:execute"`. `canonical_path` then stays at `"ggsql:execute"` (the re-export path), and `obj = get_object("ggsql:execute", loader=loader)` returns the existing Alias from the loader's static view of the package.

The function then enters its fallback branch (`obj.canonical_path != "ggsql.execute"` because the alias resolves to `ggsql._ggsql.execute`) and builds `dc.Alias("execute", obj, parent=ggsql_module)`. The new Alias has:

- `path == "ggsql.execute"` (from `name=execute`, `parent=ggsql`)
- `target` = the pre-existing Alias also at `"ggsql.execute"`

So `final_target` enters the cycle-detection set with `"ggsql.execute"`, walks to its target whose path is also `"ggsql.execute"`, and griffe raises `CyclicAliasError("ggsql.execute / ggsql.execute")`. The scan reports this as `"cyclic alias"` and the symbol is dropped from the docs.

**Classes work because** `inspect.isclass()` does return True for PyO3 classes, so `_canonical_path` returns the correct `"ggsql._ggsql:DuckDBReader"` and `get_object` fetches a concrete `Class`, not an Alias — no cycle.

**Suggested fix:** In `_canonical_path`, treat any object with a non-None `__module__` and `__qualname__` (regardless of `inspect.isfunction`) as function-like. Something like:

```python
mod = getattr(crnt_part, "__module__", None)
qn  = getattr(crnt_part, "__qualname__", None)
if mod and qn and not isinstance(crnt_part, ModuleType):
    return f"{mod}:{qn}" + (":" + qualname if qualname else "")
```

**User-land workaround that currently fixes it:** wrap the PyO3 function in a plain Python function in `__init__.py`:

```python
from ggsql._ggsql import execute as _rust_execute
def execute(query, reader):
    return _rust_execute(query, reader)
execute.__doc__ = _rust_execute.__doc__
```

The Python wrapper passes `inspect.isfunction`, so `_canonical_path` returns the right path and the cycle disappears.

---

## Issue 2 — Scan rejects PyO3 classes whose `__module__` is `"builtins"` as `"not found (likely Rust/PyO3)"`

**Location:** `great_docs/core.py:5600–5630` (the `gd_get_object(f"{normalized_name}:{name}")` validation block in `_discover_exports_via_dir`).

**What happens:** PyO3 classes by default expose `__module__ == "builtins"` (unless the Rust code explicitly sets `#[pyclass(module = "…")]`). Inside `dynamic_alias`, `_canonical_path` computes `"builtins:DuckDBReader"`, then `get_object("builtins:DuckDBReader", ...)` raises `KeyError` because `builtins` isn't in the griffe collection. The scan catches the `KeyError` and records `"not found (likely Rust/PyO3)"`.

**User-land workaround that currently fixes it:**

```python
for _cls in (DuckDBReader, VegaLiteWriter, Validated, Spec):
    _cls.__module__ = "ggsql._ggsql"
```

Or in Rust: `#[pyclass(module = "ggsql._ggsql")]`.

**Suggested fix:** If `_canonical_path` computes a canonical path whose module isn't loaded, fall back to using the path the class was *accessed* through (e.g. `ggsql._ggsql:DuckDBReader`) before declaring failure.

---

## Issue 3 — Sort of class members crashes with `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'NoneType'` when `lineno is None`

**Location:** `great_docs/core.py:6395` and `6462`.

```python
lineno = getattr(member, "lineno", float("inf"))  # line 6395
...
method_entries.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])           # line 6462
```

**What happens:** For dynamically-inspected PyO3 methods (and for aliases resolving to them), griffe sets `member.lineno = None`. The attribute *exists*, so `getattr(..., float("inf"))` doesn't fall back — it returns `None`. When two or more methods all have `lineno=None`, `sort()` tries to compare `None < None` and raises `TypeError`. The outer `except Exception` catches it, logs `Warning: Could not introspect 'DuckDBReader': TypeError` and categorizes the class as `"Other"` (in addition to the correct `"Classes"` bucket, so items show up twice in `great-docs scan`).

**Reproduction without PyO3:** any griffe object whose members are inspected (e.g. `force_inspection=True` on a regular module) will produce `lineno=None` and hit this.

**Suggested fix:** Coerce `None` to `float("inf")`:

```python
lineno = getattr(member, "lineno", None)
if lineno is None:
    lineno = float("inf")
```

There's an identical pattern for module-level members around core.py:6572 and 6605 that should be fixed too.

---

## Issue 4 — `.pyi` stubs next to a `.so` submodule are not effectively merged into the inspected version

**Location:** Interaction between `griffe._internal.finder.ModuleFinder.iter_submodules` and `griffe._internal.merger.merge_stubs` as invoked from `griffe._internal.mixins.SetMembersMixin.set_member`.

**What happens:** At the top-level package (`__init__.py` + optional `__init__.pyi`), `ModuleFinder.find_package` explicitly pairs them as `Package(path=..., stubs=...)` and `_load_package` calls `merge_stubs` on them. But for a **submodule** consisting of `_ggsql.abi3.so` + adjacent `_ggsql.pyi`, no `stubs=` is attached — both paths are yielded as separate `(name_parts, path)` entries by `iter_submodules`, and `_load_submodule` loads each in turn. The second one trips `SetMembersMixin.set_member`'s implicit-stub-merge path (mixins.py:187–199), which calls `merge_stubs(member, value)`.

`merge_stubs` then reaches `_merge_stubs_members`: when a member exists in both (the inspected `Class` from `.so` and the parsed `Class` from `.pyi`), and both are of the same kind, it calls `_merge_class_stubs`, which merges fields into the inspected object. But the inspected object *keeps its identity* — filepath, `lineno=None`, and methods with `lineno=None`. The stub's nice linenos on methods never get copied onto the inspected method objects; the stub's method objects are discarded in favour of the inspected ones because they already exist by name.

**Observable effect:** `python/ggsql/_ggsql.pyi` with real linenos (23, 24, 55, 75, 96) is parsed correctly (verified with `allow_inspection=False`), but after the full load the module's `filepath` is the `.so` and every method's `lineno` is `None`. This then triggers Issue 3.

**Suggested fix (griffe side):** In `_merge_class_stubs` / `_merge_function_stubs`, when the inspected object has `lineno=None` but the stub has a real lineno, copy it over. Same for `filepath` on the class.

**Suggested fix (great-docs side):** Independent of Issue 3, prefer `Path`-based source location from the alias's final target instead of relying on `member.lineno` to be sortable.

---

## Issue 5 — `render_docstring_section` falls through `_convert_rst_text(list)` and crashes with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'splitlines'`

**Location:** `great_docs/_renderer/_render/doc.py:472–475` → `great_docs/_renderer/_rst_converters.py:111` (`_smart_dedent` calling `text.splitlines(True)`).

**Traceback tail (reliable):**

```
File "great_docs/_renderer/_render/doc.py", line 475, in render_docstring_section
  return _convert_rst_text(el.value)
File "great_docs/_renderer/_rst_converters.py", line 140, in _convert_rst_text
  text = _smart_dedent(text)
File "great_docs/_renderer/_rst_converters.py", line 111, in _smart_dedent
  lines = text.splitlines(True)
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'splitlines'
```

**What happens:** `render_docstring_section` is a `singledispatchmethod`. It has specialized registrations for `DocstringSectionExamples`, `DocstringSectionDeprecated`, etc. For any section type without a registration, it hits the base implementation at doc.py:472:

```python
new_el = qast.transform(el)
if isinstance(new_el, qast.ExampleCode):
    return CodeBlock(el.value, Attr(classes=["python"]))
return _convert_rst_text(el.value)
```

Some section reaches this fallback with a non-string `el.value` — a `list` of something. The one-shot "unexpected text section DocstringSectionKind.text" warning that fires just before the crash (doc.py:413: `assert i == 0, f"unexpected text section {section_kind}"`) is relevant: when `_DocstringSectionPatched.transform_all` produces multiple sections and one of them is a Text section appearing at `i > 0`, the assertion fires but execution apparently continues (assertions in rendering code, or caught higher up), leaving the pipeline in a state where a list-valued section ends up at doc.py:475.

I wasn't able to isolate the exact triggering section in a minimal reproducer — rendering each of my PyO3 classes individually via `RenderDocClass` succeeds (~260 chars of valid markdown each). The crash only happens in the full `Builder.build()` pipeline when the whole reference is aggregated. Likely a page-level aggregation (multiple classes + the base Subject/Docstring assembly) is producing a combined sections list where a list-valued `.value` leaks into the fallback branch.

**Suggested investigation path for the great-docs team:**

1. Log `type(el)` and `type(el.value)` immediately before the `_convert_rst_text(el.value)` line at doc.py:475. That will identify which section type is missing a registration or is escaping normalization.
2. The "unexpected text section" assertion at doc.py:413 — decide whether it should raise or coerce; right now it fires in debug builds but is silently swallowed in release builds (Python `assert`), masking the real problem.
3. Consider guarding the fallback: `return _convert_rst_text(el.value if isinstance(el.value, str) else str(el.value))` — not a real fix but would make the crash visible as garbled markdown instead of a hard failure, which is easier to diagnose in the wild.

---

## Not-a-bug but worth mentioning

- **Scan duplicate reporting:** after Issue 3 triggers, classes are added both to `Classes` and `Other` in the scan output. Once Issue 3 is fixed this resolves itself, but it's confusing when triaging.
- **`dynamic: false` doesn't actually disable dynamic inspection in the scan path:** `gd_get_object` in `core.py:5556` and `6318` always uses `partial(qd_get_object, dynamic=True, …)` regardless of the user config. If `dynamic: false` is meant to be an escape hatch for PyO3/cyclic-alias packages (as the default config comment suggests), it should be threaded through here.

---

## Repro package

PyO3 skeleton exporting two classes (one returned from the other) plus two free functions, re-exported from a Python `__init__.py` with a `.pyi` stub alongside the `.so`. All issues reproduce with:

- `great-docs init`
- setting `module:` to the façade package
- `great-docs scan` → Issues 1, 2, 3
- `great-docs build` → Issue 5 (Issue 4 always present but silent unless Issue 3 is fixed)

title: Improve cross-referencing support: interlinks, See Also descriptions, and `%seealso` descriptions
description:
Cross-referencing between API items in docstrings needs improvement. Currently, several approaches are partially supported but incomplete.

Interlinks syntax is currently not working and doesn't resolve in builds. For this docstring:

```python
class BaseStore:
    """Base class for all stores.

    Available implementations:

    - [](`~raghilda.store.DuckDBStore`): local storage with embedding and BM25 search.
    - [](`~raghilda.store.ChromaDBStore`): local storage using ChromaDB.
    - [](`~raghilda.store.OpenAIStore`): hosted storage using OpenAI's Vector Store API.
    """
```

We should expect that each `[](`~fully.qualified.Name`)` renders as a hyperlink to the referenced item's page, showing only the short name (e.g., `DuckDBStore`). However, the interlinks filter is not active, so these render as unresolved text.

With regard to NumPy-style `See Also` sections (names link, descriptions dropped), we should expect this to work:

```python
class BaseStore:
    """Base class for all stores.

    See Also
    --------
    DuckDBStore : Local storage with embedding and BM25 search.
    ChromaDBStore : Local storage using ChromaDB.
    OpenAIStore : Hosted storage using OpenAI's Vector Store API.
    """
```

and we should expect to see a "See Also" block with linked names and their descriptions. Right now, though, names render as links, but the `: description` text is dropped during the post-render merge step.

We also support a simple `%seealso` directive (names only, no description support).

```python
class BaseStore:
    """Base class for all stores.

    %seealso DuckDBStore, ChromaDBStore, OpenAIStore
    """
```

This works right now for linking names but it has no syntax for adding descriptions.

Proposed Improvements:

1. enable the interlinks filter so that `[](`~package.Class`)` resolves to cross-reference links in docstring prose.
2. preserve descriptions in See Also sections; the post-render merge step should carry through `: description` text from NumPy/Google-style See Also entries.
3. consider description support for `%seealso`; e.g., `%seealso DuckDBStore : Local storage with embedding and BM25 search.`

title: Custom section sidebar sorts subdirectories alphabetically after prefix stripping, breaking numeric order
description:
## Summary

When a custom section uses nested subdirectories with numeric ordering prefixes (e.g. `01-foundations/`, `02-effect-estimation/`), Great Docs 0.16.0 strips those prefixes when copying files into the build tree, then sorts sidebar subsection keys alphabetically on the **stripped** names. This breaks the documented workflow where numeric prefixes control subsection order.

## Expected behavior

Per the [Custom Sections docs](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/user-guide/custom-sections.html#numeric-prefix-stripping), numeric prefixes on subdirectory names should control sidebar section order while producing clean display titles:

```
examples/
├── 01-foundations/
├── 02-effect-estimation/
├── 03-identification/
├── 04-panel-time/
└── 05-applied-models/
```

Sidebar should render in numeric order: **Foundations → Effect Estimation → Identification → Panel Time → Applied Models**.

## Actual behavior

With Great Docs 0.16.0, the sidebar subsections are ordered alphabetically by stripped slug:

1. Applied Models
2. Effect Estimation
3. Foundations
4. Identification
5. Panel Time

## Minimal reproduction

`great-docs.yml`:

```yaml
sections:
  - title: Examples
    dir: examples
    index: true
```

Source tree:

```
examples/
├── 01-foundations/page.qmd
├── 02-effect-estimation/page.qmd
└── 05-applied-models/page.qmd
```

Generated `_quarto.yml` sidebar places `applied-models` before `foundations`.

## Root cause

In 0.16.0, `_copy_section_files` strips numeric prefixes from subdirectory path components (fixing cross-ref link rewriting), so `page["filename"]` becomes e.g. `foundations/page.qmd` instead of `01-foundations/page.qmd`.

`_add_section_sidebar` then groups by the stripped parent directory and sorts with:

```python
for subdir in sorted(subdir_groups_dict.keys()):
```

Before 0.16, keys retained numeric prefixes (`01-foundations`, `02-effect-estimation`, …), so alphabetical sort preserved intended order. After stripping, `applied-models` sorts before `foundations`.

## Suggested fix

Sort subdirectories by **source discovery order** (order of first encounter while iterating the already-sorted source file list), or sort by the original prefixed path before stripping. Either preserves author intent without requiring `sidebar_groups` for every nested section.

## Workaround

Explicit `sidebar_groups` in `great-docs.yml` restores the desired order, but it is verbose and duplicates information already encoded in directory names.

## Environment

- great-docs: 0.16.0
- Observed while upgrading [pathmc](https://github.com/pymc-labs/pathmc) docs (PR #365)
